changelog: Bug 1 findings: confirmed the frontend is not at fault -- a native <input type="date">'s .value is always plain YYYY-MM-DD, never a locale- or timezone-shaped string, so the "MM/DD/YYYY-shaped value" theory doesn't hold up. The real mechanism: createSession() parsed the submitted date as UTC midnight and compared it directly against candle_sync's earliest_open_time/latest_open_time in milliseconds -- but a real exchange candle's open_time is essentially never exactly midnight UTC (it opens whenever the market/backfill actually starts, not on a human boundary). The setup form's own helper text and Start Date prefill are calendar-day truncations of that same timestamp, so the exact earliest date the UI told the user to use was numerically *before* the real earliest_open_time and got rejected by its own displayed lower bound.

Fix 1: createSession() now compares calendar days (gmdate('Y-m-d', ...) on both sides) instead of raw milliseconds. Both bounds remain inclusive, unchanged. The existing snap-to-nearest-real-candle query immediately after this check already resolves the sub-day gap correctly once a valid calendar day is let through -- verified against the exact reported scenario (earliest candle at a non-midnight UTC hour, user submits the earliest calendar day) before shipping, not assumed.

Bug 2 findings: fetched the actual deployed js/backtest.js directly from the live server (a public static asset, no auth needed) and confirmed BT_LEAD_IN_BARS=300 and the full v3.20.8 lead-in/visible-range logic were already correctly present -- this was not a deployment or caching failure. The real interaction: when a session starts at the absolute earliest candle that exists at all, there are, by definition, zero candles behind it -- no lead-in fetch, however correctly implemented, can produce history that doesn't exist. Since v3.20.6 defaults/prefills Start Date to exactly that earliest date, and Bug 1 was rejecting any attempt to use it, every session created since v3.20.6 shipped was very likely anchored at the one point in history structurally guaranteed to have no lead-in.

Fix 2 (decision, stated per instruction): default the setup form's Start Date prefill to DEFAULT_LEAD_IN_BARS (300) candles *into* history from the earliest, not the earliest candle itself -- a fixed offset into the actual available series (via LIMIT/OFFSET, immune to any real gaps), not "a recent period," which would have been a bigger, less predictable behavioral change and untethered from the lead-in count itself. New get_backtest_symbol_range field default_start_time carries this value; min/max and the 'Data from ... onward' text still reflect the true earliest/latest range unchanged, and leaving the field blank still means the literal absolute earliest candle, exactly as v3.20.6 specified -- only what the field is prefilled with changed.

Also: cache-busting added for every local JS module and both local CSS files (index.php), tied to version.json's current_version and appended as a ?v= query string -- stale cached assets have already once made it unclear whether a shipped fix had actually taken effect in this release series.
release_notes: No new migration in this release. Nothing was deployed or migrated as part of this turn, per instruction.
